key_insight: PECA reduced mean response length by 72.8% while increasing multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0% in a 1.7-billion-parameter language model.
clinical_relevance: Shorter medical responses could reduce reading burden in time-constrained workflows, but clinical usefulness and safety remain unestablished.
method: Adds a differentiable conciseness term to QLoRA supervised fine-tuning.
Encourages end-of-sequence generation after a token budget is exceeded.
Requires no preference data or auxiliary model and trains on a single commodity GPU.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports fine-tuning on medical-o1-reasoning-SFT and multiple-choice diagnostic evaluation, with a conciseness-strength sweep mapping accuracy–length trade-offs.
watch_item: Results from one model and multiple-choice evaluation do not establish whether shorter responses preserve clinically important details in real-world use.
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
